issue.title: s(269) ≤ 16.889730073596: improved packing (registration request)
issue.body:
**Credit name.** Doğa Özden ([@dogaozden](https://github.com/dogaozden), https://dogaozden.com/math/live/square-packing/); improved_by Doğa Özden. The result was found by his AI research lab. This issue and the certificate repository were prepared and posted on his behalf by his AI agent, which uses the GitHub account `kenaznia-doga`.

**Claim.** `s(269) ≤ 16.889730073596` (the exact rational side of the witness, rounded up at 12 places). The record holds ` = 16.9009945799513249` (`packing/frontier/n-269.md`, T-290, our own packing (Doğa Özden, found_by; jlevy/squares#947), built from Nate Chaoweeraprasit's packing (itsnaka) improved by Evan Daniel and PingYou Ltd). **The improvement is 1.126e-02** (relative 6.66e-04). **This improves our own jlevy/squares#947, already registered as T-290 (16.9009945799513249), by 1.1265e-2, and our own open #962 (16.8994690758550465; PR #966 is adopting it) by 9.74e-3; it supersedes both.** It is an upper bound only: no KKT, local-optimality, rigidity or global-optimality claim.

**Leaderboard, stated first.** The certified side is BELOW the Kaggle leaderboard's side-only entry for n = 269 (16.889730079125, elegans, 2026-11-05; cache of 2026-11-09, unpublished and unverifiable) by 5.53e-9; it is 1.13e-2 below the registry record, our own #947 (T-290), 9.74e-3 below our own #962 and below the best public packing we know of (16.901513582205, kirilltym). Details under "Other public values" below.

**Certificate.** A `Witness/v2` file (corners, rational scalars, 269 squares), `n-269-candidate.yaml`, in https://github.com/kenaznia-doga/s269-upper-bound-1688973007 at commit `f496016d3ebccb00c00cbf146efe85e0cc952dda` (https://github.com/kenaznia-doga/s269-upper-bound-1688973007/tree/f496016d3ebccb00c00cbf146efe85e0cc952dda). SHA-256 `35b1307a3a0dc2eb806ef064933c809a2f2b7eda73551bcc4ba6c411a307b5e6`. `n269-witness.json` is the same file as JSON. The exact coordinates were produced by this repository's own `packing-witness promote --strategy robust-rational` (@ 0352d755) from our decimal pose: `center_dilation: '1'`, no dilation, so the pair margins of about 2e-13 are the decimal pose's own (left by the final f64 repair scaling of Evan Daniel's quench, about 1e-13 relative), rounded to 36 digits. The promotion puts the least corner coordinates at 0 and takes the side as the greatest, so only the squares that set the left wall, the bottom wall and the side touch them exactly; other squares near a wall clear it by up to about 1e-12. The decimal pose is in the repository as `n-269-decimal-pose.yaml`, which the witness's `source.path` names; `certificate.replay` names the repository's own file.

**Checking.**
- This repository's `packing-witness verify` (jlevy/squares `main` @ 0352d755, run unmodified on the file placed under `packing/witnesses/known-best/`): `VERIFIED`, method exact-algebraic, 36046 pairs tested. Output in `packing-witness-verify.txt`.
- `sqcheck.py` (in the repo), our own exact checker written separately from the registry's code: `VALID`, exact rational. Output in `sqcheck-output.txt`.
- Before promotion, `sqcheck.py` also certified the decimal pose in interval arithmetic at its own side.
- The exact side minus the record's exact side is negative in `Fraction` arithmetic.
- Rerun commands are in the README.

**What the checkers share.** The unit-square, wall and non-overlap definitions only. The promotion to rationals used your tool, so `packing-witness verify` is not independent of how the coordinates were rounded; `sqcheck.py` is.

**Not done.** No local-optimality or rigidity analysis. No formal proof-assistant check. No human review outside our project. We found no open jlevy/squares issue or PR for n = 269 below the record (checked 0352d755, 2026-11-11 19:10 PST), and nothing better for it in evand/square-packing @ c801ab47 (lists/best.md: 16.9015135821891 for n = 269).

**Lineage and credit.** The record's holders as the registry lists them: Doğa Özden (found_by; our issue #947), a packing found by transplanting Evan Daniel's n = 304 packing. Found by an AI-run column-band designer, new for this filing, no donor packing (tilted squares stand in columns across a band along the diagonal at unit pitch, each column a stack of 1 to 3 squares sliding on its own; the axis-parallel squares sit on the two wall-anchored staircase lattices; for a side fraction f and band angle 45 degrees minus delta an exact dynamic programme over the columns maximises the number of squares; the best design was quenched once with Evan Daniel's ALM+SLP code, then random kicks of the coordinates and a further quench). This packing was found from a designer packing with no registry packing as a seed: design f = 0.913469, band angle 42.8° (delta 2.2°), tolerance 0, 45 tilted squares, column offset 0.96875, diagonal variant 14, quenched once to 16.890507465412 (11 s into a local run of the cloud job b2h269's command line). Fq kicks of that packing then lowered it: a kick of sigma 0.0222 and a quench gave 16.889734433328, and a further kick of the best packings so far (sigma 0.001007) gave the filed side 16.889730073596, 5 s into the kick run. (The cloud job b2h269 itself reached 16.88973007359575 by a kick, sigma 0.0265, of a parent at 16.890507620785 at 210 s, but its pack file was lost to an infrastructure fault before it could be copied, so the filed packing is the local re-find, which has the same structure and a side 9e-14 higher.) The filed packing has 45 tilted squares (the registry record has 100): one band at about 42.1° and a small cluster of squares at about -44.9° at the upper-right end. Squares matched by assignment up to the symmetries of the square: 261 of 269 centres move by more than 1e-3, 137 by more than 0.05 (largest 1.879); 121 squares are re-tilted by more than 1° (largest 44.4°); the packing has 45 squares tilted by more than 0.5° against the record's 100. See `records/n-269-candidate-diff.png`. Credit the improvement to Doğa Özden, the band's source packing to n = 207 (registry), n = 70 (Ryan Xu; improved by Evan Daniel and PingYou Ltd) and our own n = 179 (#954) and the current record to its holders as the registry lists them, and the local optimizer to Evan Daniel (`search/packer`, MIT, @ bb4cc78e).

**Licence.** The repository carries `LICENSE.md`: CC BY 4.0 for the witness, data and text; MIT for code. It also carries Evan Daniel's MIT notice, `LICENSE-evand-square-packing.txt`.

**Other public values, for context.** The best public Kaggle per-puzzle packing we found for 269 has side 16.901513582205 (kirilltym; dataset refreshed 2026-11-11 03:32Z), above ours. The Kaggle per-puzzle leaderboard (staff notebook inversion/squares-in-squares-per-puzzle-leaderboard; cache of 2026-11-09 20:52Z) lists a side-only entry for n = 269: **16.889730079125**, team elegans, 2026-11-05. It is unpublished and states no packing, so we cannot verify it and make no claim about its method. **Our certified exact side is below it: 16.889730073595636 vs 16.889730079125, by 5.53e-9** (claim 16.889730073596). The cache is from 2026-11-09 20:52Z, so a later entry may be lower. Ours is also 1.13e-2 below the registry record (our own #947, T-290), 9.74e-3 below our own #962 (16.899469075856, T-296 in the registry's draft adoption PR #966), and 1.18e-2 below the best public packing we know of (16.901513582205, kirilltym): a published packing with a certificate whose side is below the leaderboard's side-only entry.

**AI assistance.** Yes, throughout. The search and its code were written and run by AI agents; the checks above were run by code that did not produce the packing. Doğa directed the work and asked that our results be registered.

comment_on_947.body: Superseded by our new filing https://github.com/jlevy/squares/issues/967: s(269) ≤ 16.889730073596 (certified exact side 16.889730073595636, from a column-band designer; certificate https://github.com/kenaznia-doga/s269-upper-bound-1688973007), 9.74e-3 below this issue's side and below the Kaggle leaderboard's side-only entry (16.889730079125, elegans, cache of 2026-11-09) by 5.5e-9. If #962 is already being adopted (PR #966), #967 is the further improvement.
